accepted.sentence: Commercial nurseries multiply selected plants in sterile laboratory culture, producing large numbers of uniform planting specimens.
Developing bunches are often enclosed in perforated sleeves to reduce insect damage and scarring on the fruit surfaces.
Growers may brace a heavy fruit stalk with a pole or rope to keep the loaded plant from leaning or toppling.
At packing stations, workers separate harvested bunches into smaller groups and wash away sap and field debris before grading.
The flower stalk emerges from the plant’s center and bends downward, while protective bracts open successively to expose rows of flowers.
Many edible cultivars develop fruit without fertilization, as their ovaries enlarge even though mature seeds do not form.
During ripening, respiration briefly rises sharply in a climacteric phase that accompanies rapid softening.
Growers commonly replenish nutrient-demanding fields with split fertilizer applications, often supplying nitrogen and potassium during active growth.
